newsitem.title: USA: Cerner adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Cerner adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Cerner Corp said Thursday it has adopted a stockholder rights plan by declaring a dividend of one preferred stock purchase right for each outstanding share of common stock.

The plan is intended to prevent a hostile takeover without board approval. Cerner said it has received unsolicited inquiries and proposals from parties who have expressed an interest in acquiring or merging with the company.

"(C)erner is strongly committed to fulfilling the company's long-term strategy and believe any business combination at this time would deprive stockholders of the long-term value expected to be obtained as a result of implementing this strategy," the company said in a statement.

The right will be issued on December 2 to stockholders of record as of that date and will expire in 10 years. Under the plan, rights become exercisable only if a group or person acquires 15 percent or more of the company's common stock or announces a tender offer.
The right entitles the holder to purchase one one-thousandth of a share of a new series of preferred stock.

In addition, Cerner said Neal Patterson, chairman and chief executive, and Clifford Illig, president and chief operating officer, have expressed an interest in purchasing in the open market a total of up to $2 million of additional Cerner stock.

Patterson and Illig each own about 10 percent of the company's outstanding shares, Cerner said. Because of the size of their ownership, Cerner said any pooling of interests acquistion would require both Patterson's and Illig's approval.

Cerner, which provides information systems for the healthcare industry, is in the last phase of the development and rollout of its Health Network Architecture 500 platform which would allow health systems to automate and integrate clinical, operational and management activities.

"Cerner believes that HNA 500 will provide the company with a long-term competitive advantage," Cerner said in a release, adding the company has invested significantly in the product and believes it will substantially increase shareholder value over time.
